# 1.2.41 - the glass, audited end to end and then repaired

Stained Glass was taken apart in a running Foundry rather than read: 46 surfaces
photographed and measured, 263 text leaves, 756 boxes, 154 strings read off real
pixels, at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440, as a GM and as a player. Almost everything
below is a number that moved.

**Type takes back a screen term, and that one change fixed eight cuts.** On a
1080p screen the theme's geometry ran at 0.75 and its type at 1.00, so every box
was a quarter smaller with the same words in it. That ratio, and nothing else, was
why the character sheet's Actions tab overflowed by 151px, why six action tiles
were wider than the tiles they name, why the item-table list clipped its names by
22px and the chat card's header by 47. The type factor is the slider on
`max(0.85, autoScale)` now: the sheet overflows by 0 at 1440p, the tiles by 5px,
the chat header by 7. The trap that made this necessary in the first place cannot
come back - the readability floor is a plain multiply rather than a `max(1, ...)`,
so the slider still moves it: 14.3px at 80%, 25.0px at 140%.

**The curtain was cutting glass with the type scale.** `uiScale()` in the curtain
read `--drpg-sg-scale`, which is the TYPE factor; every number it feeds is a box -
the notice tile's 330x160, the Despair rail's fallback, the room the scene rail is
bounded to. Nothing showed while the two factors happened to be equal below 1440p.
It reads the geometry factor now. Together with bounding the scene rail off its own
box instead of its first tile - Foundry keeps a 33px header above that tile, and the
rail was being given it twice - the left rail with its tools open went from 66 of 80
tile corners on its own glass, 11 on a neighbour's pane and 3 on no pane at all, to
80/80 at 1440p and 77/80 with nothing off the glass at 1080p.

**One bone.** Three near-whites were on screen at the same time: Monokuma Legacy's
`#e4ded8` in 100 places, Foundry's own `#efe6d8` in 41, and the theme's declared
`#f2eee6` in 25 - the rarest, and the brightest. The other two are pointed at the
theme's for the length of the theme, which also lifts every one of those 141 strings
a little further off its background.

**The value step the floor had swallowed.** 215 of 263 visible strings sat on
exactly one size, so a label and the value beside it read as one mass. The theme's
own hierarchy was never built out of many sizes - it is plates, colour, and one step
between a label and its value - and that step is what came back. A status strip's
number now stands over its label; Health and Sanity are on the ladder instead of a
fixed 24px that ignored the interface scale; and an action tile no longer says
"1 ACTION" louder than it says "SEARCH", which it had been doing since two rounds
made two separate, defensible decisions about the same tile in two different places.

**Four colours that were failing on glass get a ground.** Contrast measured off real
pixels put 16 of 154 strings under 4.5:1, and they were not sixteen problems - they
were four: Hope's gold, the GM badge on a red tile, Despair's pink, and the accent,
each laid straight onto a transparent pane with a lit map behind it. They get what
the design's own chips get: their colour, an edge of themselves, and an opaque
ground. Strings under 4.5:1 went from 7 to 5 on the GM's side, and the two that the
probe still reports low measure 11.8:1 and 6.9:1 when computed from the colours it
itself sampled - a bitmap probe under-reads a hairline face below about 12% ink
coverage.

**Running text gets a scrim, and windows get the light back.** Liquid glass stays
the ground of every window at 0.58, which was the point of it; what changed is that a
block of running text now has something of its own directly under the letters, so a
bright patch of map stops turning into a coloured cloud beneath an empty messenger.
And a window finally looks like glass rather than a dark panel: the design's diagonal
band of light and its 0.45 top edge were never implemented, and cost two declarations.

**The pause screen is a pane.** Foundry starts paused, so this is the module's cover,
and it was wearing a 3px double gold frame with a glow ring in a theme built out of
one-pixel seams - and spending Hope's gold on something that is not Hope. The frame is
scoped back to Monokuma Legacy, where it was designed and where it is right. Stained
Glass gets the same glass as everything else, with the seam in the hour's colour.

**Things that are clicked.** 102 controls measured under 24px across 33 of 46
surfaces, and 60 of them were one control: every window's header buttons, 24x15. Now
0 under 24px. Checkboxes went 18 to 22 with the tick to match, the four Despair
steppers have names and tooltips, and nineteen leftover corner radii went to 0 -
seven of which were written inline by JavaScript with `!important` and could not be
reached by any stylesheet.

**The suite stops guessing.** `a trace and its bullets are one record` and `a trap
watches, fires once` each failed twice and passed on the very next run of the same
code. Both assert on a value that travels two hops, and the helper they waited with
is a flat 400ms - right for "nothing should have happened", wrong for "this should
have arrived". They wait for the condition now. Three consecutive runs: 119 passed,
3 failed, the same three every time.

Also: Micro 5 and Pixelify Sans were tried and rejected during the type work, and
their four woff2 files and four `@font-face` blocks stayed behind - 28.5KB every
player downloaded and no rule ever named. Gone, with the measurements that decided it
kept in the stylesheet. The GM panel's footer was 32px wider than the panel it sits
in. A dead `0.84` window ground that had not painted anything since the day liquid
glass was made the rule. And the room-reveal animation draws its lines as the same
seam as everything else - measured identical to the room border at two zooms, core
and all three glow passes - with the spreading panes between them carrying the
curtain's own stains and its pulse.

Monokuma Legacy was measured after all of it: its own bone, its own tile sizes,
opaque windows, no scrim, no sheen, no chip, and its gold title card intact.
